author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: On a moon where the former inmates of an abandoned psychiatric hospital have organized into clans by diagnosis, a marriage falls apart while Earth tries to reconquer the settlement.
page_summary:
Alpha III M2 was once a psychiatric hospital colony; cut off from Earth, its patients built a functioning society organized by diagnosis — paranoids as the ruling elite, manics as warriors, depressives, schizophrenics, and obsessive-compulsives each in their own caste. When Earth sends an expedition to bring the moon back under control, the mission tangles with the collapsing marriage of Chuck and Mary Rittersdorf.

PKD treats mental illness not as pathology to be cured but as a set of working orientations to the world, each with its own competence and blind spot. The clan system is a joke that turns serious: it asks what 'sane' organization would even look like, and whether the diagnoses that segregate people also describe the machinery of an ordinary society. The domestic warfare of the Rittersdorfs runs alongside the political plot, so that private betrayal and interplanetary reconquest mirror each other.

Written in the mid-1960s, it is one of PKD's most mordantly comic novels, folding a Ganymedean slime mold, a telepathic simulacrum, and a marital breakdown into the same off-kilter frame.
